memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'These are the regulations for a man with a discharge, for anyone made unclean by an emission of semen, for a woman in her monthly period, for a man or a woman with a discharge, and for a man who has sexual relations with a woman who is ceremonially unclean.'" - Lev 15:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a list — every situation named, nobody left out.

Look back over the whole of it. God spoke about bodies without embarrassment. He made provision for chronic illness and for ordinary monthly rhythms. He set the cost of restoration at the price of two small birds so that no one was priced out. He treated men and women alike at the altar. And He explained, at the end, that all of it existed so He could live among them.

That is a God worth knowing.

But feel the limitation too. Every one of these washings was temporary. Tomorrow it would begin again. The bath, the evening, the counting, the birds — an endless cycle that could manage uncleanness but never end it.

Which is exactly why Hebrews contrasts it with what Christ has done. The blood of goats and bulls sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that they are outwardly clean. How much more, then, will the blood of Christ... cleanse our consciences (Heb 9:13-14).

Outwardly clean, over and over. Or consciences cleansed, once and for all.

You do not live in Leviticus 15. You live on the other side of the cross.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has this chapter shown you about God's character?
2. Do you live as though your cleansing is repeated or finished?
3. What would a cleansed conscience change for you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You have done what no washing could — cleansed my conscience once and for all. Let me live today in the freedom of that finished work. Amen.
